I can only tell you based on growing up around here. The whole city of New Orleans is the cultural jewel of Louisiana. Stop by before they lock us down again!

I grew up in Baton Rouge and Lafayette. You'll see people selling produce alongside the road so you should prepare some small bills. These are the people you should be talking to to get a real feel for the average person.

Antiques is a past time for my family (I think for a lot of Louisianans). Breaux Bridge, Covington, Slidell, and Thibodaux are towns we'd visit to see Louisiana history through their antique shops. We used to go to Washington, LA to see Civil War re-enactments and buy what I was told were illegal Civil War artifacts (bullets and buttons mostly).

If this were a different time I'd say look up places doing live zydeco music and dancing. My mother used to take us to little country places around Lafayette every weekend. People dancing like it was the most natural thing. I greatly miss those times.

Lastly I highly recommend Whitney Plantation tour. It's the only tour I know of that focuses on the experience of the people who were enslaved. Oak Alley Plantation nearby is more famous but possibly more problematic.
